original_test_intent: Verify a one-shot implicit uncorrectable DRAM event for every required slot, proving exactly one mapped fault, the approved poison/fatal containment response and complete recovery with no residual armed state.
original_method: Resolve the Correctable label against errortype 1; map one physical slot to the exact tuple; define Data Poisoning state and an owned synthetic access that consumes the armed UCE; capture OOB console and pre-counters; arm mode 0 once; trigger it once; correlate exact UCE location with process/OS/machine-check/reset behavior; verify a second safe access does not reinject; recover/clean poison, prove disarm and restore state before another target.
manual_activity: The FAE resolves severity and disposition, maps the tuple, defines the consuming access, runs one UCE under OOB control, proves disarm/cleanup and restores the platform.
required_inputs: Decision that title/Criteria/errortype 1 override the Correctable step label
Tool/spec version/hash/license and implicit one-shot arm/trigger/disarm semantics
Data Poisoning state, consumption action and deterministic process/MCA/reset/fatal outcome matrix
Per-slot UCE OS/BMC/console oracle plus timeout
Poison cleanup, backup, abort, OOB recovery and restoration
safety_requirements: Dedicated backed-up SUT with independent console/power/reimage and synthetic trigger only
Do not arm until severity, poison and fatal outcome matrix are approved
One mapped UCE per approval; stop after any disruption and never advance automatically
Abort on wrong slot, repeated event, outcome outside matrix, boot loop, lost console or persistent poison
No automatic retry/recovery; prove disarm and clean poison before restoration
agent_execution_scope: Validate severity decision, topology, trigger, poison policy, package and recovery plan
Collect read-only status/counters, command, console, OS/BMC and post-recovery evidence
Do not choose target/trigger, change BIOS/HDT, arm/inject, consume poison, reset/reimage/retry or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve Correctable-label conflict and UCE outcome matrix
Approve tuple, trigger and one-shot/disarm evidence
Supervise injection and OOB recovery/poison cleanup

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title, Criteria and errortype 1 specify uncorrectable, while the injection step says Correctable. Slot 1~N is represented by fixed tuple 0:0:3; no implicit trigger or one-shot disarm proof exists. Fatal behavior is optional rather than an oracle; profiles conflict, timeout is undefined and Windows conflicts with dmesg.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The implicit one-shot UCE purpose is recognizable. Engineering can resolve labels, target, trigger and containment, so static review completes while execution is gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 51 Wistron-System RAS-00771-V002: confirm UCE coverage despite the Correctable step label; provide slot-to-tuple coverage and approve/correct 0:0:3; define implicit trigger, Data Poisoning/consume semantics, exactly-one-event/disarm proof and deterministic process/MCA/reset/fatal outcomes replacing `may`; decide DRAM-versus-MCA profile; approve tool/spec provenance, timeout, Linux/Windows/BMC/OOB evidence, poison cleanup, recovery and restoration.

review_improvement: Exposes the severity-label conflict and turns optional fatal behavior into a deterministic, single-consumption UCE checkpoint with disarm and recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Errortype 1 changes both safety and acceptance relative to the adjacent CE case, so a Correctable procedure label cannot be treated as cosmetic. Implicit UCE becomes observable only when a defined access consumes the armed fault. Because host execution and logs may terminate at consumption, the outcome matrix and OOB capture must precede arming. One-shot status also requires proving that no second injection remains after recovery.
